synopsis: Chapters 7 and 9 and the glossary agree that, assuming a homogeneous Poisson process, zero false alarms over T hours gives a one-sided upper event-rate bound of −ln(alpha)/T, approximately 3/T at 95% confidence [f5456, f6907, f14243, f6908]. Under that assumption, zero unnecessary automatic brakes in about 300 representative operating hours supports a rate below 1 per 100 hours at 95% confidence; about 3,000 hours supports below 1 per 1,000 hours [f6909, f6910]. If two events occur instead, Chapter 9 gives a 95% upper rate bound of about 6.3/T [f6911]. These assurances are conditional: false alarms can cluster by site, weather, machine, obstacle geometry, contamination, bucket passes or dust clouds, and can be non-stationary, so the homogeneous-Poisson assumption must be checked before relying on the bound [f5459, f6913, f6915].
